source.title: Dense ideals in topological algebras: some results and open problems

accepted.question_text: Let A be a commutative unital complex m-convex B0-algebra, meaning a completely metrizable locally convex algebra whose topology can be given by a sequence of submultiplicative seminorms. Must every multiplicative linear functional on A be continuous? Equivalently, must every codimension-one maximal ideal of A be closed?

evidence.quote: Unless otherwise stated, all algebras in this paper will be commutative, complex, unital, with the unity denoted by e.
– The class MB0 = MLC ∩ F of all m-convex B0-algebras, where the relations (4) are replaced by (2).

Problem 1. Let A be a commutative unital m-convex B0-algebra. Is it true that all its multiplicative-linear functionals are continuous ? In other words: is it true that all maximal ideals of A of codimension one are closed ?

accepted.question_text: If A is an F-algebra that is also a division algebra, must A be isomorphic to the complex field C?

evidence.quote: – The class F of all F-algebras, i.e. completely metrisable topological algebras.
Problem 2. Is it true that a division algebra of type F is isomorphic to C ?

accepted.question_text: Let A be a commutative complex unital B0-algebra, that is, a completely metrizable locally convex algebra. Must every multiplicative linear functional on A be continuous?

evidence.quote: Unless otherwise stated, all algebras in this paper will be commutative, complex, unital, with the unity denoted by e.
– The class B0 = LC ∩ F of B0-algebras, their topology is given by means of a sequence of seminorms
Problem 3. Let A be be a commutative algebra of type B0. Is it true that all its multiplicative-linear functionals are continuous ?

accepted.question_text: Let A be a commutative complex unital F-algebra, meaning a completely metrizable topological algebra. Does it follow that every multiplicative linear functional on A is continuous?

evidence.quote: Unless otherwise stated, all algebras in this paper will be commutative, complex, unital, with the unity denoted by e.
– The class F of all F-algebras, i.e. completely metrisable topological algebras.
Problem 4. Let A be a commutative algebra of type F. Does it follow that all its multiplicative-linear functionals are continuous ?

accepted.question_text: Suppose A is an F-algebra with continuous inversion on its group G(A) of invertible elements. Must A have no proper topologically invertible elements, where an element x is topologically invertible if there exists a net (z_α) in A with z_α x converging to the identity e, and where a proper topologically invertible element means an element of G^t(A) that is not actually invertible?

evidence.quote: We say that an element x in A is topologically invertible if there is a net (zα) ⊂ A such that limα zα x = e.

The set (group) of all invertible elements of A will be denoted by G(A) and the set of topologically invertible elements – by Gt(A). In general, it is only a multiplicative semigroup and it contains G(A). The proper topologically invertible elements are defined as elements of Gt(A) \ G(A).
Problem 5. Suppose that an F-algebra has a continuous inverse. Does it follow that is has no proper topologically invertible elements ?

accepted.question_text: Suppose a topological algebra A has a dense finitely generated ideal I = x1 A + · · · + xn A. Must A contain a proper topologically invertible element? More strongly, must the ideal I itself contain a topologically invertible element?

evidence.quote: The proper topologically invertible elements are defined as elements of Gt(A) \ G(A).

Problem 6. Suppose that a topological algebra has a dense, finitely generated ideal I = x1A + · · · + xnA. Does it follow that A has proper topologically invertible elements ? We can ask also a stronger question, whether the ideal I must have a topologically invertible element.

accepted.question_text: Let A be a topological algebra with the Arens property, meaning that A has no dense finitely generated ideal. If A0 is a closed subalgebra of A, must A0 also have the Arens property?

evidence.quote: We say that a topological algebra A has the Arens property if it has no dense finitely generated ideal.
Problem 7. Let A be a topological algebra possessing the Arens property and let A0 be its closed subalgebra. Does it follow that A0 has the Arens Property too ?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist an F-algebra, or even a B0-algebra, in which every proper ideal is dense?

evidence.quote: Problem 8. Does there exist an F-algebra (or even a B0-algebra) with all (proper) ideals dense ?
